# Rung N (`rung-nat-checker`): the first skeptic's judgement

**Verdict: refused.** The one thing that must change: two behaviours this rung repairs are not pinned by any gated assertion, and the three-homes rule puts both in home 1. (a) The `ExportChecker.equalIntExprs` edit (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala:645-646`) has no test at all. With only that file taken back to `47437c65f`, a component that exports its own api with a sized function is refused with "Missing declarations: {unbox[\nat k\](b:SkSizedApi.Box[\k\]):ZZ32 ...}", and with the edit it checks clean (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/skeptic/export-ab.txt:3-11`). (b) `XXXNatArithChecker.test` says `compile_err_contains=Arithmetic on nat static arguments is not supported by the type checker`. That string is in the declaration-level message and in the use-site message alike (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-nat-checker/probes/skeptic/junit-rerun.txt:101-102`, `:107-108`), so the use-site check that REPORT.md section 6 counts as home 1 (`TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:144-145`) could be deleted and the test would stay green. Each needs a gated assertion that goes red without its edit, and that has to be shown before the next judgement. Everything else below is a correction for the same repair round, or a recommended row.

Inherited state: branch `wip/rung-nat-checker` at `6ee779492`, five worker commits past `47437c65f`, working tree clean. `ProjectFortress/build` is newer than every edited source (the Scala classes date from 02:02:23, and the last source edit, `OverloadingOracle.scala`, is from 02:01:32). The five library components are in `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache`. I did not rebuild. All my runs used `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` on one machine: nproc 4, Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.80GHz, 2800.212 MHz, JDK 25. The load average at the start of each run is in the first lines of its capture. I recorded no timings of my own.

## 0. The provenance block

input.summary: Refused once. Most of the claim is true. The recorded failure exists: commit 9e014be3e holds the tests and junit-before.txt and no source edit, and all nine tests are red at NI.nyi or at the ClassCastException. All ten tests and the size regression tests pass when I re-run them. The count table reads 125 with crash row none, and the report, the record, the structured report and the prediction all say 125. The provenance block's five lines all check out. The SubOvSwap acceptance is the shape the batch record excepts. Two home-1 repairs are ungated: the ExportChecker edit, which I measured as load-bearing with a one-file A/B, and the use-site arithmetic check. My differential of 30 programs of my own found five further things. (1) The multiple instantiation exclusion covers type arguments only: g(Tg[\3\]) beside g(Tg[\4\]) on a trait is refused, while the type twin is accepted and runs compiled, printing 3 and 4. (2) A generic call whose ZZ32 parameter takes a numeral is refused when static arguments are inferred. This predates the rung for types and sizes now reach it. (3) In an overload set, the rung's no-context rule drops a dead-size arm from static resolution while run-time dispatch still selects it. SkDeadVal is accepted and dies compiled with NoClassDefFoundError SkDeadVal$n. (4) The bool/dim/unit named error hides every other error in the component. (5) Provisional row 388's method half duplicates ledger row 21.
differentialsRun: SkSquare (trace[\nat n\](Mat[\n,n\]) on 3x3 and 3x4): walk 7 then a refusal at run time; checker refuses the 3x4 call; agree
SkMixed ([\T, nat n\] inferred together; Vec[\String,4\] bound to Vec[\String,5\]): walk four, w, then a refusal; checker refuses only the binding; agree
SkIntKind (int parameters; IBox[\5\] bound to IBox[\6\]): walk 7, 8, then a refusal; checker refuses only that binding; agree
SkExtends (object O extends T[\3\] passed as T[\4\]): walk 7 then a refusal; checker refuses f4(O); agree

SkUnion (unbox of if c then Box[\3\] else Box[\4\]): walk 1, 1; checker refuses the OR(Box[\4\],Box[\3\]) argument; the specification types the call statically and walk checks no types, so nothing is owed
SkCtx (a size from the expected type only, with its type twin): walk fails for the type twin (BOTTOM); checker refuses both kinds alike; agree
SkRetEsc / SkRetEscT (a free size or type only in the less specific return type): walk refuses the overloading; checker refuses both alike; agree

SkCapture / SkCapDecl / SkCapDistinct / SkCapOne / SkCapDeclT (the return-type rule with shared and distinct parameter names): walk runs; checker refuses the pair in every variant; SkCapture's apparent acceptance was phase masking behind a call error; no name capture
SkOrder (a size before a type parameter): walk h; checker refuses only the bad pair hb; agree
SkNoSize2 (no size): walk refuses at run time; checker refuses the same binding, identically before and after the edit; no move
SkLitOverload (g(Box[\3\]) and g(Box[\4\]) on an object): walk 3, 4; checker accepts; agree
SkLitTrait (the same on a generic trait): walk refuses; checker refuses with 'Invalid overloading'; agree
SkLitTraitT (type twin on a trait): walk refuses; checker accepts and the compiled run prints 3, 4; the checker treats sizes and types differently here (checkP handles STypeArg only); recommended row

SkLitArgT / SkLitArgN (a generic call whose ZZ32 parameter takes a numeral): walk 6 on every call; checker refuses the inferred call as not applicable to IntLiteral, while the written-out and non-generic calls pass; the same before the edit for types; the specification converts at arguments (conversions-coercions.tex:101-102); recommended row
SkDeadN / SkDeadT (a dead parameter at a call, size and type): walk 4, 4 and 4; checker refuses both; agree on the checker side

SkDeadArm / SkDeadArmT (a dead-size arm beside dd(ZZ32)): walk 2, 1; the size version refuses dd("s") as no context; the type version accepts and the compiled run prints 2, 1; sizes are stricter than types, which the report does not say

SkDeadTop / SkDeadTopT (the dead arm is the more specific one): walk 1, 2; checker accepts both and the compiled runs print 1, 2; the no-context rule drops the arm statically and run-time dispatch still selects it

SkDeadVal (the same with body = n): walk 'undefined variable [n]'; checker accepts; the compiled run dies with NoClassDefFoundError SkDeadVal$n; the specification is silent (inference.tex:15) and Pavol's rule calls an unknown size that reaches a value an error; recommended row
SkBoolArm (a bool-generic arm beside g(ZZ32), calling g(5)): walk 5; checker refuses the program at the declaration's bool b; a named limit

SkBoolMany / SkBoolCtl (a bool inference call plus two ordinary type errors): walk refuses at run time; checker reports 1 error with the bool call and the 2 others when the argument is written out; the thrown TypeError hides the rest
api/SkSizedApi + SkSizedUse (a component exporting a sized api): walk 7; checker and compile clean; with only ExportChecker reverted, 'Missing declarations'; the edit is load-bearing and ungated
harness re-run of the ten tests plus AfterTypeChecking, XXX1p, XXX5z, Compiled12.invariantInference, NatArgRungSLink and XXXNatArgRungS: all green (junit-rerun.txt)
